covers: JSE close and the first 90 minutes of the US session, 19 Nov 2026
headline: Wall Street gives back its opening gains: S&P 500 slips to 7,309.85 as AMD falls 7.7%; rand weaker at R17.44/$ after the SARB's 4–3 hold
summary: The JSE All Share closed at 106,216.5 on 19 Nov 2026, 5.5% lower on the week, and the rand weakened further to R17.44 per dollar by 18:02 SAST after the SARB held the repo rate at 7.25% on a 4–3 vote (LRC Market Dashboard; BusinessTech, 19 Nov 2026). In New York the early rally faded: at 18:02 SAST the S&P 500 was at 7,309.85, down from 7,378.18 at 17:02, and the Nasdaq at 24,501.91 from 24,802.73, with AMD down 7.7% while Intel (+4.8%) and Palo Alto Networks (+5.0%) held gains (LRC Market Dashboard and Stock Scanner quotes, 18:02 SAST). Gold was at $3,684.50 and Brent at $89.62, while the US 10-year yield eased to 5.06%; the turn lower keeps pressure on risk assets and the rand into the US close.

items.title: SARB holds repo rate at 7.25%; MPC split 4–3, with three votes for a hike
items.summary: The Reserve Bank kept the repo rate at 7.25% on 19 Nov 2026. Four members voted to hold and three for a 25bp increase. Kganyago said near-term inflation is above 5%, in line with this week's 5.2% CPI reading, and that high prints are expected to last into early next year before easing. He said the committee is pausing "for now" and "will not hesitate to raise rates if needed" to bring inflation back to the 3% target. The close vote keeps a further hike on the table at the next meeting.
